The scene: a shabby one-room flat in an unfinished concrete panel apartment block. A big part of the back wall is missing: a large ragged hole with broken bricks and bent rebar around it, through it a view of the town with unfinished grey panel blocks, a construction crane and a small comet with a glowing tail in the hazy sky. A yellow rubble chute leads from the hole down to a pile of rubble, yellow and black warning tape hangs loosely across the hole. On the left a crooked wooden shelf unit, completely empty and dusty except for one small framed photo, no books on it. On the wall a proud wall of fame: thirteen small framed diplomas with red wax seals, hanging slightly askew in rows, one bare nail where a fourteenth is missing, and a framed chart with a single long teal bar. A wobbly wooden trestle table with a few loose papers and an old teal rotary telephone with a curly cord, no mug and no cup on the table. On the right a rust-brown apartment door hanging a little crooked in its frame, with a brass knob, several envelopes and bills pushed through the gap under the door lie on the floor in front of it. A bare light bulb hangs on a wire from the ceiling. Walls like in the reference images: ochre plaster above, a faded teal painted band below with peeling patches, plus visible concrete panel joints and a few exposed pipes.
The left and right outer sixths of the image show only walls and floor, nothing important.
Warm muted palette of ochre, rust and faded teal with yellow construction accents, simplified exaggerated shapes, nothing is perfectly straight, bold thick dark-brown outlines around every object, flat colors with simple soft shading, moderate amount of detail, clear open walkable floor in the lower quarter of the image, flat even ground plane, no fisheye lens distortion, not realistic, no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no people
